checks.title: pcpi_wait stays asserted until pcpi_ready
checks.behavior: If resetn=1, pcpi_valid=1, pcpi_wait=1 and pcpi_ready=0 at a rising edge of clk, then at the next rising edge either pcpi_wait=1 or pcpi_ready=1. pcpi_wait must not drop while an accepted instruction is still running and pcpi_ready has not been asserted. Disabled while resetn=0.

checks.title: pcpi_wr only together with pcpi_ready
checks.behavior: If resetn=1 and pcpi_wr=1 at a rising edge of clk, then pcpi_ready=1 at the same rising edge. A result is written only when execution completes.

checks.title: pcpi_ready only in response to an outstanding pcpi_valid
checks.behavior: If pcpi_ready=1 at a rising edge of clk, then resetn=1 and pcpi_valid=1 at the same rising edge. Under the legal stimulus, the master holds pcpi_valid until it samples pcpi_ready. So the DUT never signals completion when no instruction is outstanding.

checks.title: Idle after reset: no completion without an instruction
checks.behavior: After a synchronous reset and with no instruction issued, the DUT does not signal completion or write a result.
checks.stimulus: Drive resetn=0 for 5 rising edges with pcpi_valid=0, pcpi_insn/pcpi_rs1/pcpi_rs2 at random values. Then drive resetn=1 and keep pcpi_valid=0 for 50 more rising edges while pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2 change randomly every cycle (including valid DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU encodings).
checks.expected: From the first rising edge after resetn is released and on every edge for all 50 idle cycles: pcpi_ready=0 and pcpi_wr=0. pcpi_wait=0 on every idle edge once 2 edges have passed after release.

checks.title: PCPI handshake: early pcpi_wait, then pcpi_ready with pcpi_wr
checks.behavior: For each supported division instruction, the DUT asserts pcpi_wait soon enough that the core's 16-cycle illegal-instruction timeout cannot fire. It keeps pcpi_wait high until completion, then asserts pcpi_ready together with pcpi_wr.
checks.stimulus: After reset, issue each of DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU (opcode 0110011, funct7 0000001, funct3 100/101/110/111, random rd/rs1/rs2 fields) with random nonzero pcpi_rs2 and random pcpi_rs1. Drive pcpi_valid=1 with pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2 stable from the issue edge until the edge where pcpi_ready=1 is sampled, then drive pcpi_valid=0 on the next cycle. Leave 0, 1 and 5 idle cycles between instructions.
checks.expected: For every instruction: (a) pcpi_wait=1 or pcpi_ready=1 is sampled at one of the first 16 rising edges after the edge where pcpi_valid was first sampled high. (b) From the first edge with pcpi_wait=1 until the completion edge, pcpi_wait=1 on every edge. (c) pcpi_ready=1 is sampled exactly once per issued instruction, within 200 rising edges of issue (timeout = failure). (d) At that same edge, pcpi_wr=1. (e) No pcpi_ready or pcpi_wr pulse occurs while pcpi_valid=0.

checks.title: Directed DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU results incl. rounding toward zero and remainder sign
checks.behavior: pcpi_rd at the completion edge equals the RV32M result. Quotients round toward zero, and a nonzero signed remainder has the dividend's sign.
checks.stimulus: Using the CHK-005 handshake, issue these (rs1, rs2) operands: DIV/REM (7,2), (0xFFFFFFF9,2), (7,0xFFFFFFFE), (0xFFFFFFF9,0xFFFFFFFE), (0xFFFFFFFA,3), (0,5), (0x80000000,1), (0x7FFFFFFF,0x7FFFFFFF). DIVU/REMU (0xFFFFFFFF,2), (0x80000000,0xFFFFFFFF), (7,2), (5,7), (0xFFFFFFFF,1).
checks.expected: At the edge with pcpi_ready=1 and pcpi_wr=1, pcpi_rd equals: DIV 3, 0xFFFFFFFD, 0xFFFFFFFD, 3, 0xFFFFFFFE, 0, 0x80000000, 1. REM 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 0, 0, 0. DIVU 0x7FFFFFFF, 0, 3, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF. REMU 1, 0x80000000, 1, 5, 0.

checks.title: Constrained-random division against reference model
checks.behavior: Back-to-back random division operations all complete and return results matching a 32-bit reference model.
checks.stimulus: After reset, issue 5000 instructions. Pick each from DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU at random. Draw pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2 at random, weighted toward 0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0x7FFFFFFF, small magnitudes and powers of two (division by zero included at low weight). Use random rd/rs1/rs2 instruction fields and random 0..3 idle cycles between instructions. Hold inputs stable until pcpi_ready=1, as in CHK-005.
checks.expected: Every instruction gets exactly one pcpi_ready=1 within 200 edges, with pcpi_wr=1 at the same edge. pcpi_rd equals the reference: trunc(rs1/rs2) for DIV (signed) and DIVU (unsigned), and rs1 - q*rs2 for REM/REMU. Each nonzero REM result has the same sign bit as pcpi_rs1. Divide-by-zero and overflow cases follow CHK-008/CHK-009.

checks.title: Division by zero
checks.behavior: Division by zero returns a quotient with all bits set and a remainder equal to the dividend (L=32).
checks.stimulus: Using the CHK-005 handshake, issue DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU with pcpi_rs2=0 and pcpi_rs1 in {0, 1, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x12345678}.
checks.expected: Each instruction completes with pcpi_ready=1 and pcpi_wr=1 at the same edge, within 200 edges. pcpi_rd = 0xFFFFFFFF for DIV and DIVU. pcpi_rd = pcpi_rs1 (the dividend) for REM and REMU.

checks.title: Signed division overflow
checks.behavior: Dividing the most-negative integer by -1 returns the dividend as the quotient and 0 as the remainder.
checks.stimulus: Using the CHK-005 handshake, issue DIV and REM with pcpi_rs1=0x80000000 and pcpi_rs2=0xFFFFFFFF. As an unsigned contrast, also issue DIVU and REMU with the same operands.
checks.expected: DIV: pcpi_rd=0x80000000. REM: pcpi_rd=0x00000000. DIVU: pcpi_rd=0x00000000. REMU: pcpi_rd=0x80000000. In each case pcpi_ready=1 and pcpi_wr=1 at the same edge, within 200 edges.

not_verified.note: This binds the master (PicoRV32 core). The DUT is the PCPI slave. It is used as a stimulus constraint in CHK-004..CHK-009: pcpi_valid is asserted with pcpi_insn/pcpi_rs1/pcpi_rs2 and held stable until pcpi_ready.
The register-file write-back is done by the core, not the DUT. The DUT side (pcpi_rd value when pcpi_wr=1) is checked in CHK-006..CHK-009.
Raising the illegal-instruction exception is core behaviour. Its 16-cycle bound is used as the acknowledge deadline the DUT must meet in CHK-005(a).
How the core reacts to pcpi_wait is master behaviour. The DUT's pcpi_wait timing is covered by CHK-001 and CHK-005.
MUL is not implemented by picorv32_pcpi_div (a division/remainder coprocessor).
MULH/MULHU/MULHSU are not implemented by picorv32_pcpi_div.
This is a recommended software code sequence. There is nothing to observe at the DUT.
This is a register-allocation constraint on software. Multiply is also not implemented by this DUT.
This is an optional microarchitectural fusion of multiply, which this divider DUT does not implement.
MULW is RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32 (pcpi_rd is 32 bits).
This is an RV64 software usage note for MUL. It does not apply to a 32-bit divider.
This is a recommended software code sequence. Each DIV/REM is still checked on its own in CHK-006/CHK-007.
This is a software register-allocation constraint. The DUT does not write registers, and the rd field is ignored at the PCPI interface.
Optional fusion (MAY) of div+rem is an internal microarchitectural choice. Results are still checked per instruction in CHK-007.
DIVW/DIVUW/REMW/REMUW are RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32.
REMW/REMUW sign extension is RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32.

assumptions: The DUT implements only the RV32M division instructions DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU with XLEN=32 (based on the module name and the 32-bit pcpi_rd). It does not implement the multiply instructions.
Instruction encodings follow the standard RV32M R-type format: opcode 0110011, funct7 0000001, funct3 100=DIV, 101=DIVU, 110=REM, 111=REMU.
The result is presented on pcpi_rd with pcpi_wr=1 at the same rising edge where pcpi_ready=1, matching how the PicoRV32 core samples the PCPI response.
The spec gives no exact division latency, so a 200-cycle completion timeout is used as the failure bound instead of an exact cycle count.

Legal master stimulus holds pcpi_valid, pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2 stable from issue until pcpi_ready=1 is sampled, and deasserts pcpi_valid on the following cycle. pcpi_valid is never withdrawn before pcpi_ready.

The spec gives no reset values ('See specification'), so only the no-completion-when-idle behaviour after reset is checked (pcpi_ready=0, pcpi_wr=0). pcpi_wait is expected to be 0 after a 2-cycle settling window.
